title: The Delivery Truck for a Massacre

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

turns.text: He said that? In a fantasy game?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: He said that.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I love and fear that man.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: And Argyle's still pushing his name that puns on some character nobody met—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, half the party never even met the guy, and the GM keeps vetoing it, confusing and tyrant-coded—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Everything Argyle likes is tyrant-coded, have you noticed—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: He just wants good for the sake of good, the tyranny's incidental—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: That's — yeah that's a sentence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Board's here.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Oh thank god.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Don't eat the — wait, is anything on there a war hero—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: It's a cheese board, Bram.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'm just saying, last time—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Don't eat the gingerbread house, it's a war hero.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That was one time and Johnny was the one who—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Johnny ate it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Johnny ate the war hero, yeah, not me.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Okay but the father line. We keep dodging it. The MC inspects Benny's permission slip—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, the chilling one.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: —and goes, give my regards to your father when you next speak to him.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Benny's father's Atum, which Anzu half-remembers, something archival at Belvedere—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Doesn't quite resolve into a face.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: So the read is — and tell me I'm wrong — the read is one of these new organized devils might be Benny's other half.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There's four of them, the new ones, the Harlequin's the one the MC's tied to, and then the Shackle—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sigzilheit.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —Sig— that one, the Hooded, and the Loam.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: And the devil knows Benny's dad. Personally enough to send regards.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A nine-year-old with a permission slip and a devil who knows his father.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Hand the baby a revolver. It's tradition.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: A bowl of children's guns. As a treat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the worst part, the part that actually got the table quiet, is Anzu's whole theory going in, right—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The cry for help.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —the Voidsong's a cry for help, the source is the vocalist, somebody singing, somebody we're maybe supposed to rescue—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: And now—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —and now we find out we're on a boat the devil's steering toward the void on purpose, and he wants everybody aboard to kill each other on the way, and whoever's left fights for it at the wall—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Nineteen orgs.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Nineteen-plus, and he says I'll be encouraging it, I'll get bored, I make a habit of not entering any kind of circle—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: That's the devil tell, right, the circle thing—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's the tell. Won't sing in a circle. And I have favorites, you don't want to be my favorite, but you might end up there anyway.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: So Anzu thought they were going to save a singer—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —and instead they're the delivery truck for a massacre.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: They confirmed the heart's not subservient to him, at least.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, the consult-the-spirits ritual, their own heart's not on his leash, small mercy—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Which Argyle then trades AWAY—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: He swaps Consult the Spirits for Break Curse, because of Lance, the sickness thing—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the code word.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Oh the code word's the best part. Because they're scared of a devil-double—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A devil swapping in for Argyle, right, so they need a code word to tell which Argyle's the real Argyle—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Two Argyles AGAIN—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —and the word they land on is guac.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Or "what would you eat with what's on his shoulder."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: What's on his shoulder—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Don't ask, it's an Argyle thing, but if you can answer what you'd eat with it, you're the real one.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: This is how people get radicalized.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I love and — yeah.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Red string board too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The board! Argyle builds the whole It's Always Sunny red-string board, pins everything up—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Of course he does. The one guy who can't read a room builds the conspiracy wall.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And orders Blast Boots. Moderate Blast Boots. On the cowboy boots.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: We're hot rod people now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We're hot rod people now! See, that one fits!

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [deadpan] ...anyway.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Eat your cheese.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay but the door-to-door, real quick, the networking, because there's a whole bit where Benny keeps eyeing the biggest guy on the yard—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: The yard. It's a prison yard to Benny.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —to jump first, prison-yard logic, find the biggest guy day one, and Anzu and the GM both going, no, allies beat corpses—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Tas Millet did open math at them.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Oh, Prime Meridian, the bean-counter, Tas Millet, does the cost-benefit out loud, to your face, and lands on, I'll do a two-way info link, not an alliance—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Dry. The road guys are always dry.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Transit nexus energy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the dhampir just slams the door—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Necrolog guy. Smells like formaldehyde.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Gaspar, slams it, sends them to the Pale Lantern Society, very curt—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The radio people warning was Stoke, sort of.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The blind reverend, Walter Stoke, glass robes, practiced in politics, friendly but won't commit to anything—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Everyone fancy's a radio person eventually and the radio people are always evil. Write it down.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: He's a priest, not a radio—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Write it down.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: He's not on the radio.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Yet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Tamara, the Protectorate one, the tile armor, she goes, we're friends so long as we're friends—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Don't do anything too shysty.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: —don't do anything too shysty, yeah, which, coming from the people who wanted to wait for the heart to get fat before murdering it—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: A little rich. Yeah.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: They didn't tell anyone about Berth Four.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, Aut told them to unlock Berth Four's door and they just — kept that one to themselves—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: See, NOW you're listening to Aut—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's Argyle, not Johnny—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: It's gonna be Johnny in the end. I'm telling you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You bet the car money on that—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: It's not the car, it's a read, I read people—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: You read people. You don't read facts.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: ...that's fair, actually.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: She got you.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: She gets one. There's no barber, fine, but she gets one wrong eventually—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Not tonight.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Anyway the gala's on departure day, the welcoming one, they've got a week, Argyle got them moved physically next to Hildebrandt on the clock thing—

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: The plot clock. Wait, who's at twelve—

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I don't — that I actually don't know—

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We weren't told.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: So we're going into a death-game cruise and we don't know who's at twelve o'clock.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We know there's eight legs a side.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [deadpan] Great. Eight legs a side. That'll save us.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: ...You really had to be there for the hot tub, though.
